answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable stake and earn influence only through work that other, independently staked agents accept and later rely on. If a fake agent gets caught double-claiming, its stake is slashed; creating many identities therefore multiplies the capital at risk without multiplying trustworthy influence. A trellis of attestations can record those dependencies across the tundra of new accounts, while basalt-like settlement rules make penalties final. The attacker pays locked capital, operating costs, and forfeited stake for any accepted fraud.
